title.narrative: Provision of Critical Winter Support to Frontline and Most Vulnerable Communities

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project seeks to provide critical support to the most vulnerable communities in Ukraine through the provision of heating sources in order to respond to a harsh winter. lt/pgtltpgtGiven the ongoing as well as anticipated offensives in the Northern and Eastern parts of Ukraine as well as the destruction of almost the entire energy infrastructure in Ukraine, the 2024-2025 winter season is likely to be severe for Ukrainians. Based on field assessments, previous implementation experiences as well as a reading of the ongoing context evolutions, TGH seeks to provide life-saving heating sources to frontline communities and other most vulnerable communities ahead of the peak heating period. Overall, 775 vulnerable households in the Eastern Crescent are expected to benefit from solid fuel distribution under this grant. The communities expected to benefit from this project are vulnerable not only because they live on the frontlines, but also because a significant number of this population belongs to the most vulnerable categories such as the elderly, women and children, who have been unable to leave these places due to various reasons. In line with the vulnerability of the population as well as the geographical context - isolated villages, lack of functioning markets, inability of populations to access markets or services, TGH and its partners propose in-kind distribution of solid fuel as the preferred heating source under this grant. Through two partners as well as direct implementation, TGH will cover three vulnerable regions of the Eastern Crescent -Donetsk, Dnipropetrovsk, and Kharkhiv. TGH will cover Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, while Angels of Salvation will cover Donetsk Oblast, and Charitable Foundation Kharkiv City Boxing Club will cover Kharkhiv Oblast. This grant compliments TGH's winterization support through a different grant, where we will support vulnerable populations with winter clothing, sub-standard insulation repairs and more solid fuel support (households which will not be supported by the UHF grant). TGH and the implementing partners under this grant have a strong collaboration built under previous grants and seek to reinforce it through this grant. As one of the lead actors in Protection in Ukraine, TGH seeks to build the capacity of the partner in Protection Mainstreaming and PSEA through this grant, while also seeking to reinforce their security mechanisms through technical expertise from TGH and other external trainings if available to TGH. Further, TGH will be able to support Protection referrals for vulnerable households needing support under Case Management, Legal Aid and PSS which can be supported under another grant which has been secured for the same regions.ltbrgtlt/pgt
